output.source_comparison: Both rely on official Federal Reserve information. Kalshi specifies the published upper bound; Polymarket specifies the FOMC statement, with the Fed's open-market page also identified as publishing the level and change. No explicit source fallback hierarchy is provided.
output.deadline_comparison: Kalshi expires at the first 2:05 p.m. Eastern Time following the statement's release or one week after the meeting's last day. Polymarket may resolve when the statement is issued; if none is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, it resolves to No change. Polymarket's listed settlement timestamp is not stated as the rule-based deadline.
output.boundary_comparison: Kalshi YES requires an upper bound strictly greater than 3.50%; exactly 3.50% is not YES. Polymarket YES concerns a decrease of 50 or more basis points versus the prior level, with unlisted changes rounded up to the nearest 25 basis points. The supplied rules do not fully clarify rounding at every boundary.
differences: Kalshi tests an absolute post-meeting rate; Polymarket tests the size and direction of the change from the prior rate.
Polymarket specifies a no-statement fallback to No change; Kalshi gives an expiration deadline but does not specify the resulting payout if no statement is released.
The contracts have different listed close and settlement times, and different rule-based deadlines.
Cancellation, ties, and 50/50 payouts are not specified in the supplied rules.
output.explanation: The YES conditions are materially different and are not exact complements: their relationship depends on the prior rate and the meeting outcome. The supplied text also leaves cancellation and some fallback and boundary details unresolved.
